 JUDGMENT
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. This miscellaneous first appeal under Section 30(1) of Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) is filed by respondent No.2- Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 21.01.2017 passed in E.C.A.No.133/2014, by which the Commissioner for Employee's Compensation and the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Kalaburagi ('the Tribunal' for short) allowed the claim petition filed by petitioners granting compensation in a sum of Rs.8,39,757/- with interest at 12% p.a. and directed respondent No.2 Insurance Company to pay the same.
3. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. FACTS:
Brief facts leading to filing of the claim petition are that petitioners are the parents of deceased Sharanappa.

He was 22 year old working as cleaner in lorry bearing registration No.MH-25/B-7806 ('the offending vehicle' for short) belonging to respondent No.1 on monthly salary of Rs.4,500/- and daily batta of Rs.100/-.
On 11.06.2011, at about 1.00 p.m., deceased was traveling in offending vehicle from Solapur towards Hyderabad.
Near Naladurga village on Aliyabad bridge, the driver of the offending vehicle lost control over the same and dashed against another lorry bearing registration No.MH-12/AQ-7806.
In the said accident, deceased Sharanappa and driver of the offending vehicle sustained grievous injuries.

They were shifted to Government Bajaj Allianz Through vs Laxmibai W/O Mallanna Sangolgi And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402438/
2 Hospital, Naladurga and thereafter, deceased Sharanappa was treated at Ashwini Hospital, Solapur.

Despite prolonged treatment, he died on 20.06.2011 at about 11.20 a.m.
5.
Petitioners have spent Rs.1,25,000/- towards medical expenses.

In respect of the said accident,
case was registered in Crime No.79/2011.
The death of deceased occurred arising out of and in the course of employment of respondent No.1.
At the time of accident, the offending vehicle was covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.2.
As the employer and insurer, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
6. Respondent No.1 has appeared and filed written statement admitting that deceased Sharanappa was working under him as a cleaner in the offending vehicle on a monthly salary of Rs.4,500/-.
He has also admitted that the death of Sharanappa was arising out of and in the course of his employment and as such, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation.
7. Respondent No.2 has also filed written statement disputing the relationship of employer and employee between respondent No.1 and deceased.
Respondent No.2 has specifically claimed that at the time of accident, the deceased was not traveling in the offending vehicle and he did not sustain any injuries in the said accident.
It is the driver of the offending vehicle alone who sustained injury as per the FIR and spot panchanama.
Since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, respondent No.2 is not liable to indemnify respondent No.1 and prays to dismiss the petition as against it.
8. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
9. In support of the claim of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 is examined as PW-1 and Exs.P-1 to P- 7 are marked.
10. On the other hand, on behalf of respondent No.2, one witness is examined as RW-1 and Exs.D-1 to D-4 are marked.

11. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.8,39,757/- and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same with interest at 12% p.a.
12.

Being aggrieved by the same, respondent No.2 has filed this appeal contending that the Tribunal is not justified in allowing the claim petition by answering issue no.1 in affirmative, without appreciating the fact whether the death of the deceased was as a result of the injuries sustained in the accident or not.
The Tribunal has not appreciated the evidence on record in proper prospective and erroneously held issue No.1 in the affirmative.
The Tribunal has failed to frame issue as to whether the death of the deceased was arising out of employment or not, though respondent No.2 has specifically taken such a defence.

As per the post mortem report, the death of the deceased was due to pulmonary consolidation with pleural effusion and as per the radiological opinion, the deceased had bilateral active pulmonary koch's disease (Tuberculosis) which apparently proves that the death of the deceased was a result of pulmonary koch's disease and not as a result of the injuries Bajaj Allianz Through vs Laxmibai W/O Mallanna Sangolgi And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402438/
3 sustained in the accident.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has not appreciated this fact.

12.1 It is further contended by the respondent No.2 that Tribunal is not justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month contrary to what was pleaded by the petitioners and admitted by respondent No.1.
The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is opposed to law probabilities and evidence on record.

13. In the light of the specific contentions raised by respondent No.2, the appeal is admitted on the following substantial question of law:
i) Whether the Workmen's Compensation Tribunal is justified in law in holding that the death of the deceased was arising out of and during the course of employment?
14.
Heard elaborate arguments of both sides and perused the records.
15. At the outset, it is relevant to note that respondent No.2 has disputed the relationship of employer and employee between respondent No.1 and the deceased Sharanappa.

However, the contention of the petitioners that deceased was employed by respondent No.1 in the offending vehicle as cleaner is admitted by respondent No.1, though he claims that he paid only a sum of Rs.4,000/- as his monthly salary and not any batta as claimed by the petitioners.
It is true that respondent No.1 has not produced any document to show that deceased was engaged by him in his lorry.
It appears that respondent No.1 is owning only the offending vehicle and he has not maintained any registers regarding payment of wages, attendance etc.

However, this Court does not find any reason not to believe the contention of the petitioners as well as stand taken by respondent No.1 that the deceased was engaged by him in the offending vehicle as cleaner.
Therefore, the findings of the tribunal that there is relationship of employer and employee between respondent No.1 and the deceased Sharanappa is accepted.

15.1 The next ground urged by respondent No.2 is that the death of deceased was not due to the accidental injuries sustained by him but he was suffering from Tuberculosis and as such, it cannot be accepted that the death of deceased was arising out of and in the course of employment.

In order to demonstrate this ground urged by respondent No.2, it has relied upon the FIR and contended that in the FIR reveal only the fact of driver being injured in the accident is forthcoming and not any other person present in the offending vehicle.

It is relevant to note that according to the complaint averments, the complainant and others were traveling in lorry bearing registration No.MH-12/AQ-7806 which was moving ahead and it was hit by the offending vehicle being driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner.

In the complaint, the complainant has stated that due to the impact the lorry bearing registration No.MH- 12/AQ-7806 fell off the bridge and the driver of the offending vehicle also was injured and he could hear his moaning sound.
It is also relevant to note that immediately after the accident, the driver of lorry bearing registration No.MH-12/AQ-7806, who was injured, lodged the complaint.
15.2 Having regard to the fact that he had sustained grievous injuries, he may not be able to know whether apart from driver, any other person was inside the offending vehicle.

Therefore, only based Bajaj Allianz Through vs Laxmibai W/O Mallanna Sangolgi And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402438/
4 on the complaint which was filed at the earliest point of time

However, after conducting thorough investigation,
the Investigating Officer has filed the charge sheet wherein the fact of presence of deceased inside the offending vehicle in his capacity as cleaner is forthcoming and that while undergoing treatment,
Sharanappa died due to the injuries suffered in the said accident.

Admittedly, the driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged the charge sheet which also contains the allegation that due to his rash and negligent driving, the cleaner of the offending vehicle also died.

15.3 Respondent No.2 has also relied upon the post mortem report to contend that death of Sharanappa was due to pulmonary consolidation with pleural effusion and not on account of the injury sustained by him in the motor vehicle accident in question.
The medical reports together are marked as Ex.P-7.

The Chest Radiograph (Supine) dated 14.06.2011 state that a homogeneous parenchymal lesion is seen in right apical lung - suggestive of collapse/consolidation, multiple nodular lesions are seen scattered throughout the lungs.?
It is suspected pulmonary tuberculosis (Page 64).
The Chest Radiograph (Supine) dated 16.06.2011 gives a finding that possibility of Pulmonary Koch's disease likely.
The M.D.C.T. Scan Head - plain study states that finding suggestive of cerebral oedema which may be due to injury or due to inflammation due to infection.
The Chest Cardiograph (Supine) dated 17.06.2011 concludes finding suggestive of Bilateral Active Pulmonary Koch's disease which means active tuberculosis of lungs of both sides.
Similarly, the Chest Radiograph (Supine) dated 18.06.2011 is suggestive of A.R.D.S/ Koch's etiology (Page 55).

Similarly, the Chest Cardiograph (Supine) dated 20.06.2011 state that peribronchial infiltrates seen bilaterally with cavity in right upper lobe, Segmental collapse noted in right upper lobe - suggestive of extensive pulmonary Koch's disease, Right sided loculated pneumothorax noted in right lower zone. (Page 41).
15.4

The EEG and brain map analysis dated 13.06.2011 (Page 39) indicate that there is evidence of epileptic activity in the form of spikes or sharp wave discharges, interdischarge slowing seen,
hyperventillation could not be undertaken, photic stimulation was uneventful.
The impression is "This is abnormal EEG record showing generalized epileptic spike and wave discharges, Please note that normal EEG does not rule out clinical diagnosis of epilepsy".
15.5 Despite all these findings, the X-ray of left femur -AP/LAT/Pelvis with both hips reveal intertrochanteric fracture neck of femur.
LT.Ankle- AP/Lateral reveal fracture of medial maleollus.
Similarly, Chest radiograph (PA/Supine) reveal a heterogeneous parenchymal lesion in right apical region-S/o contused lung.
It may be a sign of injury to the lung or because of injury to the lungs.

15.6 From the medical evidence placed on record, it indicates that deceased was suffering from tuberculosis and in the accident, he has also sustained fracture and the accidental injuries sustained by him, accelerated his death due to pulmonary consolidation with pleural effusion.
In the circumstances, it cannot be ruled out that on account of the injury sustained by him, his condition worsened leading to his death.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered opinion that the death of deceased was due to the injuries sustained in the accident arising out of and during the course of his employment.

Considering all these evidence, the Tribunal has rightly accepted the contention of the petitioners that deceased died due to the injuries sustained arising out of and in the course of his Bajaj Allianz Through vs Laxmibai W/O Mallanna Sangolgi And Ors on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191402438/
5 employment.

sentences.text: Now coming to the quantum of compensation awarded.

It is true that petitioners have pleaded that deceased was earning Rs.4,500/- per month and in addition, he was getting batta of Rs.100/-
per day.
However, respondent No.1 who is the employer of the deceased has pleaded that he was only paying Rs.4,000/- to the deceased by way of his salary.

However, while calculating the compensation, the Tribunal has considered his salary at Rs.4,500/- per month and batta of Rs.100/-
per day i.e, in all, deceased was drawing total wages in a sum of Rs.7,000/- per month.

Based on it,
the Tribunal has calculated the compensation.

Of course, the petitioners have failed to place any material on record to show that deceased was getting salary of Rs.4,500/- per month and in addition to it, he was also getting batta in a sum of Rs.100/- per day i.e., Rs.3,000/- per month.
17.

However, Section 4 of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 deals with the criteria for calculating the compensation in case of death or permanent total disability or permanent partial disability/temporary disability, etc.

Section 4(1)(b) provides that the Central Government may by Notification in the official Gazette specify, for the purposes of sub-section (1), such monthly wages in relation to an employee as may be considered necessary.

As per this provision, with effect from 31.05.2010 vide Order No.S.O 1258(E) dated 31.05.2010, the Central Government has specified for the purpose of sub-section (1), the monthly wages as Rs.8,000/-.
Based on it, the income is required to be taken at Rs.8,000/- instead of Rs.7,500/- taken by the Tribunal.

18. Earlier, Explanation-II to Section 4 provided that where the monthly wages of workman exceeds Rs.4,000/-, his monthly wages for the purposes of Clause (a) & (b) shall be deemed to be Rs.4,000/-
only.
In other words, even where the monthly income of the workman exceeded Rs.4,000/-, as per Explanation-II it was required to be limited to Rs.4,000/- and compensation was to be determined.
However, by Act 45 of 2009 Explanation-II is omitted.

Thus, after the omission of Explanation-II,
the minimum wages which is required to be taken into consideration is as fixed by the Central Government under Section 4(1)(b).

If the parties are able to establish that the wages received by the workman exceeded the amount specified by the Central Government, the same may be considered or else it shall not be less than what is fixed by the Central Government under Section 4(1)(b).
Having regard to this provision, the Tribunal has erred in considering the minimum wages of deceased at Rs.7,500/-.
It ought to have taken the wages of deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.
19. Thus, as per Section 4 of the Act which is amended w.e.f 31.05.2010, the minimum wages that is required to be taken into consideration is Rs.8,000/- per month.
However, in the present case, the Tribunal has considered his wages at Rs.7,500/- per month.
Since the petitioners have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is no need to revise the compensation payable to the petitioners.
Therefore, the calculations made by the Tribunal in computing the compensation by taking Rs.7,500/- as wages of the deceased is correct and it requires no interference.

20. Thus, from the above discussion, I hold that the conclusions arrived at by the Tribunal that the deceased was employed by respondent No.1 and he died during the course of his employment on account of the injuries sustained in the accident in question cannot be interfered with.
